item.title: Moment two workers are pulled alive from Nepal tunnel
item.description:
Officials say pair were rescued from Trishuli 3A hydropower tunnel in Nepal after being trapped at depth of 170 metres Two people have been pulled out alive from a hydropower tunnel in Nepal nine days after deadly flash floods buried the projects in deep mud and left them trapped. The workers were rescued during an operation at the Trishuli 3A tunnel, a hydropower project in one of the areas worst affected by last week’s floods , according to the army spokesperson Brig Gen Raja Ram Basnet. item.title: Russian drone strikes Ukraine’s security service headquarters
item.description:
A Russian drone struck the headquarters of Ukraine's SBU security services on Friday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said, accusing Moscow of aiming directly at the SBU head's personal office. Zelensky said he had instructed the SBU to deliver an "appropriate, tangible response" to the strike, while Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga described it as a "major escalation". FRANCE 24's Emmanuelle Chaze reports from Kyiv, Ukraine.

item.title: In the White House's Retro Arcade Games, the Trump Administration Always Loses
item.description:
If your legal status in this country isn't dependent on keeping your job, you might want to run out the clock this Friday afternoon by playing the minigames on offer at the White House's new online arcade . These government-issued games are essentially MAGA reskins of old 2D classics. There's Rio Run , a Snake -like game where a suit-wearing enforcer collects as many brown-skinned border crossers as possible into a chain behind him while attempting to avoid collision with the borders of the game and his own captives. Once players have had their fill of active border enforcement, they can transition to Build the Wall , essentially the Trump administration's version of Tetris . In a slight twist on the classic game, the goal here is to stack falling four-block shapes into the highest possible border wall. item.title: Philippine vice president is ordered arrested for threats against the president
item.description:
Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte arrives before the start of her impeachment hearing at the Philippine Senate in Metro Manila on July 7, 2026. —Noel Celis—Pool/Getty Images A Philippine court on Friday ordered the arrest of Vice President Sara Duterte over alleged grave threats to her former ally, President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. , his wife, and a former House Speaker. The warrant against Duterte, 48, set the bail at 120,000 pesos ($1,900) for each of the three counts against her. “Regardless of the question on jurisdiction, she has no intention of evading the law and will continue to exercise all her legal remedies,” Duterte’s lawyer said in a statement . Duterte has been charged with threatening the lives of Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and his cousin, former House Speaker Martin Romualdez. item.title: Gloria Steinem: A life in pictures
item.description:
For years, when interviewers asked for a favorite quote, I gave them Gloria Steinem’s: “We are linked, not ranked.” She used the line in 2013 as shorthand for her whole political vision. Women are not a tournament. We are not climbing over one another toward a single chair. We thrive when we treat our connection as a circle instead of a hierarchy. I needed that line. In corporate life in the 1990s and early 2000s, the conventional wisdom held that there was room for only a few of us in executive team rooms and that the smart play was to swat the woman next to you out of the way. Steinem’s sentence rejected that scarcity story. The problem was the ranking, not the other woman. I am a feminist. I adopted the word in college. Before that I was an athlete training eight hours a day, with no political opinions to speak of. What I had was a body that coaches treated as theirs to break and use…

item.title: UN votes to adopt new world map to reflect Africa's true size
item.description:
Togo-sponsored resolution called to phase out traditional map that depicts continent as similar size to Greenland The United Nations has voted to adopt a resolution for the world to formally phase out the traditional Mercator map of the globe in favour of one that more accurately displays Africa’s size. In a session at its headquarters in New York, the UN general assembly officially retired the 16th-century Mercator projection in favour of one based on the more accurate 2018 Equal Earth design.
